detection.summary: The OLT scan reports seven failed PONs and an offline population well above baseline despite a healthy aggregate status, while sampled active customers have missing cached optical readings but normal historical optics and active service.

diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is down: all eight ONU probes on the held port returned responds=true with online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and MPCP DEREG. The OLT itself is healthy and responsive, so this is a PON port failure rather than an OLT failure. The healthy aggregate status is inconsistent with the failed-PON detail and live outage evidence.
evidence: The OLT ping, SNMP, and OID subtree all respond successfully.
The held interface resolved to EPON0/7, and all eight queried ONUs returned responds=true with online=0, establishing definite offline states.
The two sampled line-specific queries returned online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and exchange=MPCP DEREG.
The port customer view identifies the affected lines on EPON0/7 and shows onu_status=0 with cached rx_power=0.
The OLT population has 43 of 272 customers offline, above the 4.85% baseline, consistent with a real service outage rather than normal background.
OLT CPU, memory, and temperature trends remain near healthy baselines, and both VLAN probing and customer VLAN 1047 are correct.
Historical optical series for both sampled lines were normal: RX ended at -21.28 dBm, TX at 2.33 dBm, distance remained constant at 166, and TX bias remained within the healthy range.
Cached zero optical values are not valid signal measurements; live offline probes correctly return null optical readings.
diagnosis.discrepancy_detail: Cached ONU optical values are rx_power=0 and tx_power=0, while live queries return null because the ONUs are definitely offline. The stored healthy aggregate status also conflicts with the failed-PON detail and live EPON0/7 outage.

remediation.reason: EPON0/7 has a confirmed port-wide outage affecting multiple ONUs, while the OLT and optical histories are healthy. This indicates a PON port failure rather than an individual ONU, fibre, or OLT failure.
remediation.instructions: Escalate to the infrastructure team to test and restore EPON0/7, including port hardware, optics, and OLT interface configuration. Validate ONU re-registration and service recovery after remediation. Treat cached zero optical values and the healthy aggregate status as stale or inconsistent telemetry.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The outage affects all queried ONUs on the same PON port, so resetting individual ONUs would not address the common failure.
Historical optical levels and distance are stable, with no evidence of fibre degradation, distance change, or splitter failure.
Multiple ONUs failed simultaneously and there is no evidence of laser ageing or individual ONU hardware failure.

escalation.summary: EPON0/7 has a confirmed port-wide outage affecting eight queried ONUs. All probes report offline, unauthenticated, and MPCP deregistered, while the OLT remains responsive and healthy. Escalate to infrastructure to test and restore the PON port, including port hardware, optics, and interface configuration, then validate ONU re-registration and service recovery. Cached zero optical readings and the healthy aggregate OLT status are invalid or inconsistent telemetry.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
